docs.text: Slipstream Financial documentation A practical starting guide for maintaining the Slipstream Financial WordPress website. Where to make changes What you want to update WordPress location Homepage and page sections Pages → select the page → Edit Articles, categories and featured images Posts Images and uploaded files Media → Library Header, footer, blog hero defaults and inner-page hero Appearance → Customize Navigation links Appearance → Menus Lead form fields and messages Forms (Gravity Forms) Before you start To request the website’s login URL or account access, contact your Coalition Technologies project team. Once you receive access, sign in using your assigned account. Available menus depend on your permissions. This site uses a custom theme with ACF Pro blocks in the WordPress block editor. Select a section in List View to locate its fields. Preview your changes, check the page on desktop and mobile, then use Update , Save or Publish , as shown in your editor. Start with Editing pages , Homepage , or Header, footer and menus . Site map at a glance Verified against the local WordPress admin (November 19, 2026): Area How it is set up Homepage Settings → Reading → static front page Home Blog listing Posts page Blog ( /blog/ ), layout from the theme Solution / marketing pages Mostly the Inner Page template + ACF blocks Lead / contact pages Contact Lead block + Gravity Forms Header / footer chrome Appearance → Customize (not page blocks) Production URLs and any staging-only pages still need a final check on the live site. See Developer handoff . About this guide This base was checked against the local theme source on November 10, 2026, and extended from theme source plus the local WordPress admin on November 19, 2026. Screenshots were captured from the local admin with account menus and private fields obscured where needed. It covers implemented controls and templates. Production hosting, notification recipients and plugin licensing still need confirmation by the team. Do not store credentials, private email addresses or license keys in this public repository.

docs.text: Blog and resources Edit an article Go to Posts → All Posts and select an article, or choose Add New . Maintain the title, body, categories, excerpt and featured image, then preview and save. The theme renders the article header and content through its single-post template. A Blog Inline CTA block is available for a call to action inside an article, with a headline, CTA label, CTA URL and background image. Listings and categories The posts page is selected under Settings → Reading → Posts page . In the local admin this is the published Blog page. The theme supplies the blog hero and listing layout (you do not edit those listing cards inside the page body). Category archives use the same layout family, filtered to the category. Manage categories through Posts → Categories and assign them in each post’s settings. The local site’s active article category is News . Listing behavior from the theme: About six posts per page on the blog index and archives Featured images appear on listing cards and in the single-post hero (theme fallbacks apply when an image is missing) Related articles on a post page are chosen by category Blog hero defaults Open Appearance → Customize → Blog Hero to edit the label above the headline, headline, intro and optional background used on the posts index. Category archives use the category name and description instead of those Customizer copy fields. On the local site the label above the headline is set to Knowledge Base . The Customizer overview below shows where to find Blog Hero . Open that section to see its editable fields. Resources template The Resources page template also renders the blog layout. Listing cards still come from WordPress posts. In the local admin the Resources page is trashed; confirm on production whether editors should use Blog , a restored Resources page, or both. Developer follow-up: confirm production posts-page URL, category labels, sticky/featured behavior and removal of any remaining sample content.

docs.text: Forms The Homepage Hero and Contact Lead blocks integrate with Gravity Forms . Each has a Gravity Form ID field. The homepage hero also exposes an optional form-shortcode field; ask the developer to confirm its use before replacing an existing setup. Forms in use (local admin) Verified in the local WordPress admin (November 19, 2026). Confirm the same IDs on production before relying on them there. Form ID Form title Typical placement 1 Homepage Hero Homepage Hero block ( Gravity Form ID ) 2 Contact Lead Contact Lead blocks on contact / talk / demo pages Theme options mirror those IDs ( Homepage Hero → 1, Contact Lead → 2). Field labels editors usually maintain Both forms include First Name, Last Name, Email, Company Name and Message. The Contact Lead form also includes a CAPTCHA field. Edit labels, required flags and placeholder text inside Gravity Forms — not inside the page block. Form title/subtitle text that appears above the inputs on the page still comes from the Homepage Hero or Contact Lead block fields. Basic maintenance Open Forms in WordPress and identify the form used by the page. Edit its fields in Gravity Forms. Review confirmations and notifications in the form settings. Keep the page block’s Gravity Form ID matched to the intended form. Save and test the form on the front end, including required-field errors and the confirmation message. Form headings in the page block are separate from form input labels. If the form does not render, have the developer verify plugin activation and the selected form ID. Confirmations and notifications Configure confirmation messages and notification routing inside each form’s Gravity Forms settings. Notification recipient addresses, API keys and spam-service credentials must stay in WordPress admin only — never commit them to this public documentation repo. Developer follow-up: confirm production form IDs, notification delivery, integrations and spam protection after checking the live configuration.

docs.text: Homepage Open the homepage Check Settings → Reading to identify the page assigned as the homepage, then open it under Pages . In the local admin this is the published page titled Home . The theme supports editable ACF homepage blocks. It also has a fallback layout rendered from theme defaults when homepage block content is absent. If the editor is empty but the front end shows sections, ask the developer to populate the editable blocks before making content changes. Section order Keep this order unless a deliberate layout change is planned. Verified on the local Home page: Homepage Hero Stats Bar Services Grid Operations Features Mission Tabs Finley CTA Industries Carousel Nexus Platform Video Spotlight For an illustrated example of selecting blocks and opening their fields, see Basic block editing . Available homepage sections Section Main content fields Homepage Hero Label above headline, headline, subcopy, background, form title/subtitle, Gravity Form ID, optional form shortcode, service cards (label, icon) Stats Bar Metrics (value, label) Services Grid Headline; cards (title, copy, CTA label/URL, image, wide card, panel position) Operations Features Headline, copy, columns; features (title, copy, icon) Mission Tabs Headline; tabs (tab label, panel title, copy, CTA label/URL, image); tags Finley CTA Headline, copy, dense layout, button label/URL, banner background, Finley image Industries Carousel Headline, copy; cards (title, URL, image) Nexus Platform Label above headline, headline, lead, body, image; checklist items Video Spotlight Label above headline, headline, copy, video file or URL, poster image Editing a section Open Home and use List View (Document Overview). Select the existing block — do not insert a second copy of the same section. Edit fields in the Block sidebar, or use Open Expanded Editor for longer fields and images. For repeaters (cards, metrics, tabs, checklist rows), edit existing rows first; preview after adding, removing or reordering. Preserve <span> or <strong> tags inside headlines when they mark highlighted words. Preview on desktop and mobile, then save/update the page. Some empty fields still display theme fallback images or structure, so clearing a value may not remove every visual element from the page. Homepage form The hero’s form title and subtitle belong to the Homepage Hero block. Form inputs, required rules, confirmations and notifications belong to Gravity Forms . On the local site the block’s Gravity Form ID points to form 1 — Homepage Hero .

docs.text: Header, footer and menus Header Open Appearance → Customize → Header . Available settings include: Logo and sticky header. Header CTA label and URL. Header email link. Phone display text and phone link. The overview below shows the available sections. Select Header to open the controls described above. Update the visible phone number and its tel: link together. The email link uses a mailto: address. Do not publish private addresses in this documentation repository; maintain them only in Customizer. Footer Open Appearance → Customize → Footer to edit the about/blurb text, primary and secondary CTA labels/URLs, support email, sales email and copyright line. The theme also uses shared logo and phone settings. On the local site the primary footer CTA points at the Request a Demo page and the secondary CTA at Talk to a Specialist. Preview the result and use Publish to save Customizer changes. Inner page and blog defaults Also in Appearance → Customize : Section What editors change Inner Pages Fallback hero background and compact hero minimum height Blog Hero Label above headline, headline, intro and optional background for the posts index Navigation Open Appearance → Menus , choose the menu and edit its links. Drag child items beneath their parent to create dropdown items, then save. Menu items may also have an optional Menu icon (Media Library image) used in mega-menu dropdowns. The theme registers these menu locations. Local admin assignments: Location Purpose Local menu Primary Menu Header navigation Primary Footer — Knowledge Base Footer knowledge links Footer — Knowledge Base Footer — Payment Solutions Footer solution links Footer — Payment Solutions Footer — Legal Footer legal links Footer — Legal Footer Menu (legacy) Compatibility location; confirm usage before assigning Unassigned locally Check location assignments under Manage Locations . Header/footer buttons are controlled in the Customizer, separately from menu links.

docs.text: Editing pages Go to Pages → All Pages and open the page. Open List View to locate the existing section. Select the block and edit its ACF fields; switch to the block’s editing mode if it is showing a preview. For lists such as cards, logos or steps, edit the existing repeater rows. Preview after adding, removing or reordering rows. Preview links, images and spacing, then save the page. Templates Inner Page adds a hero above the page content. It uses the page title, excerpt and featured image, with an Inner Page Hero field group for the label, headline override, button and background. The Customizer’s Inner Pages section supplies a fallback hero background and compact hero height. Most solution, about, contact and lead pages in the local admin use Inner Page . Resources renders the theme’s blog hero and post listing. Its layout is composed by the theme; editing the page body does not control that listing. The local Resources page is currently trashed — the public posts listing is the Blog page under Settings → Reading . Confirm whether a Resources page should be restored on production. Avoid changing an existing page’s template without checking the preview. Solution page sections The local Modern Banking & Treasury Solutions ( banking-treasury ) page uses the Inner Page template. Its hero is rendered by the template above the content blocks; it is not a Solution Hero block in List View. This was confirmed against the active theme and the local page’s saved template and block content on November 19, 2026. Edit the Banking & Treasury hero Open the page under Pages → All Pages and keep its Inner Page template selected. Edit the page Title for the default headline, or use Inner Page Hero → Headline override . Edit the page Excerpt for the hero description. In Inner Page Hero , edit Label above headline , Button and Background as needed. These are page-level fields, not a content block. Change the page’s Featured image for the hero’s side image. The background falls back from the page’s Background field to its featured image, then the Customizer/theme default. Preview and save the page. Do not add a Solution Hero block to this page: the Inner Page template already renders its hero, so a separate hero block would create a second banner. The standalone Solution Hero block remains available for other layouts that require it. Content blocks below the hero The saved Banking & Treasury page contains these blocks: Section Main fields Logos Strip Headline, intro; logos (image, alt, URL); marquee toggle Process Steps Headline, copy; steps (tag, title, copy, image) Video Copy Split Headline, intro, body; checklist; poster; video file or URL; play label Trust Image Cards Headline, copy; cards (image, title, copy) Platform Tags Split Label above headline, headline, media, card title, tags, card copy Feature Duo Headline, copy; features (icon, title, copy); side image Finley CTA Same fields as on the homepage Local banking-treasury body stack (below the Inner Page hero): Logos Strip → Process Steps → Video Copy Split → Trust Image Cards → Platform Tags Split → Feature Duo → Finley CTA. Other useful sections: Team Grid — headline, intro, members (photo, name, role, bio) Contact Lead — headline, intro, list intro, bullets, body, form title/subtitle, Gravity Form ID Lead-style pages such as Talk with a Fintech & Payments Expert and See SlipStream in Action combine process/content blocks with Contact Lead . Prefer editing the existing Contact Lead block rather than adding another form block. Images and links Choose images through the Media Library and provide useful alternative text for meaningful images. Check button labels and destinations together. Preserve existing headline formatting when editing fields labeled “HTML allowed”; it may control the highlighted words. Basic block editing: illustrated example These screenshots show the local Slipstream WordPress admin using an unpublished demonstration page and the real Finley CTA block. Placeholder text is for demonstration only. They are not a published production page. 1. Choose a custom block Use the + Block Inserter in the top toolbar. Custom blocks appear under CT Theme ; search by name or choose Finley CTA . On an existing page, select its existing block instead of adding a duplicate. 2. Select a block and find its fields Open Document Overview in the toolbar, then List View . Select Finley CTA . The Block settings on the right show its headline, copy, CTA label and URL. If the sidebar is hidden, open Settings . 3. Use the expanded editor Click Open Expanded Editor for a larger field panel. Edit the text and button destination; use Add Image for the banner or mascot. Preserve existing <span> tags in the headline to retain highlighted words. Empty image fields can still display theme fallback artwork. Click Done to return to the canvas. This closes the panel; it does not save the page. Use Save draft for an unpublished page, or the editor's save/update control for a published page. Preview before publishing.

docs.title: Basic block editing: illustrated example

docs.text: Use the + Block Inserter in the top toolbar. Custom blocks appear under CT Theme ; search by name or choose Finley CTA . On an existing page, select its existing block instead of adding a duplicate.
docs.title: 1. Choose a custom block

docs.text: Open Document Overview in the toolbar, then List View . Select Finley CTA . The Block settings on the right show its headline, copy, CTA label and URL. If the sidebar is hidden, open Settings .
docs.title: 2. Select a block and find its fields

docs.text: Click Open Expanded Editor for a larger field panel. Edit the text and button destination; use Add Image for the banner or mascot. Preserve existing <span> tags in the headline to retain highlighted words. Empty image fields can still display theme fallback artwork. Click Done to return to the canvas. This closes the panel; it does not save the page. Use Save draft for an unpublished page, or the editor's save/update control for a published page. Preview before publishing.
docs.title: 3. Use the expanded editor
